metaTitle: Winneba Masquerade Festival (Kaakaamotobi) on New Year’s Day
metaDescription: The Winneba Masquerade, or Fancy Dress Festival, fills Winneba with masked dancers and brass bands every 1 January. Its history, the five clubs and how to go.
ogTitle: The Winneba Masquerade: New Year’s Day in masks
subtitle: Masks, brass bands and a contest on New Year’s Day
answer: The Winneba Masquerade, known locally as Kaakaamotobi and often called the Fancy Dress Festival, is held in Winneba every 1 January. Five masquerade clubs parade in masks and elaborate costumes to brass band music and compete in a march past and dance contest, making it the first big festival of the year in Ghana.

sticky.title: New Year’s Day
sticky.text: The clubs parade on 1 January every year: no waiting for a council announcement.

sections.title: Where the masquerade comes from
sections.html:
Masquerading came to Ghana’s coastal towns through contact with European traders and colonisers, who brought masks and fancy dress to their celebrations. Winneba took it up and formed its own masquerade groups as far back as the 1930s.[[1,2]]

In 1957 Kwame Nkrumah, Ghana’s first president, formalised the tradition and sponsored the first parade to celebrate independence. The festival has run every New Year’s Day since, for more than sixty years.[[1]]

sections.title: The five clubs
sections.html:
Five groups take part, each with its own colours, costumes and band: Nobles No. 1, Egyaa No. 2, Tumus No. 3, Red Cross No. 4 and Royals No. 5.[[1]] They spend months making masks moulded into faces that are meant to frighten, or to make the crowd laugh, and the name Kaakaamotobi comes from those moulded masks.[[1]]

The masquerade was traditionally for men, and many still dress up as women in wigs, earrings and gowns. Women now take part too.[[1]]

days.label: Morning
days.title: Into the streets
days.html: The clubs come out in costume, with stilt walkers and brass bands, and parade through Winneba.[[1,2]]

days.label: Afternoon
days.title: March past and dance contest
days.html: At the park, each group marches past and dances for the judges, and the best are rewarded.[[1]]

sections.title: Good to know if you go
tips: Where: Winneba is on the coast road between Accra and Cape Coast. The contest is usually at Advanced Park.
When: it’s on New Year’s Day. Roads out of Accra are busy after the night’s celebrations, so leave early.
Photos: the masqueraders love an audience, but ask before close-ups and give stilt walkers room.
Also in Winneba: come back in May for Aboakyer, the deer hunt.

faq.a: Every year on 1 January, New Year’s Day.
It is the local name for the Winneba Masquerade, from the moulded masks the masqueraders wear.

faq.q: How many masquerade clubs are there in Winneba?
faq.a: Five: Nobles No. 1, Egyaa No. 2, Tumus No. 3, Red Cross No. 4 and Royals No. 5.
